title: FedProphet: Memory-Efficient Federated Adversarial Training via Robust and Consistent Cascade Learning
problem: Federated Adversarial Training (FAT) requires large models to attain high accuracy and robustness, but memory-constrained edge devices cannot fit full-model training; existing memory-efficient FL methods sacrifice accuracy or robustness through objective inconsistency between local and global models.
motivation: Edge devices in federated learning have limited DRAM. Adversarial training further increases memory by requiring multi-step PGD attack generation during each forward-backward pass. Partitioning the model into cascaded modules reduces per-device footprint, but naive partitioning causes the local module objective to diverge from the global adversarial objective.
method: FedProphet uses adversarial cascade learning: the full model is split into small sequential modules, each trained on one class of devices. Strong convexity regularization on each module's loss ensures local module objectives remain consistent with the global adversarial loss. A server-side coordinator performs Adaptive Perturbation Adjustment (APA) to balance utility vs. robustness trade-off dynamically, and Differentiated Module Assignment (DMA) to assign modules to heterogeneous devices, mitigating objective inconsistency across rounds.
key_novelty: Cascade learning with strong convexity regularization that simultaneously achieves memory efficiency and adversarial robustness in federated settings, proven to imply low objective inconsistency, combined with APA and DMA coordinators on the server.
contributions: Adversarial cascade learning framework partitioning large models into memory-fitting modules for FAT
Strong convexity regularization guaranteeing global robustness from local module training
Server-side Adaptive Perturbation Adjustment for utility-robustness balance
Differentiated Module Assignment to handle heterogeneous device memory across federation rounds
80% memory reduction and up to 10.8x speedup over joint FAT (jFAT)
hardware_target: Memory-constrained edge devices (federated); server-side coordination node
workloads: Federated adversarial training on image classification (CIFAR-10, Caltech-256)
limitations: Cascade partitioning introduces inter-module communication rounds that add latency
Strong convexity assumption may not hold for all model architectures
Evaluated on image classification only; NLP tasks not addressed
